newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia businesses expectations rise in Q4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia businesses expectations rise in Q4.

text.p: Australian business expectations for the next year improved in the December quarter, while current business conditions remained subdued, a survey found.

"The results of the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry's (ACCI) national survey of business expectations show there has been an increase in business confidence during the past quarter," the survey said.

"However, in terms of the actual level of activity, the plain and obvious fact is that the economy has been very subdued with little indication that economic conditions had picked up during the quarter just completed," it said.
This was reflected in actual results for general business conditions, sales revenue, profitability, employment and overtime, the survey report said.
ACCI chief executive Mark Paterson said there had been a slight increase in the level of sales for only the second time since May 1995.
The survey said this indicated it may be the end of a period of prolonged stagnation.
But Paterson said there had been a fall in other economic indicators with business conditions, profitability, employment and overtime showing a negative net balance in the last quarter.
"There has been a further slowing in price movements with more firms recording a fall in prices than an increase," Paterson said in a statement.
The survey said there was no indication of a rise in inflation while wage movements appeared to have slowed.
"Investment continues to show positive growth although there appears to be some slowdown occuring," Paterson said.
The survey said both the actual and expected levels of investment were lower now than they were in the same period last year, but expectations for private investment continued to be positive.
The survey shows the results of a sample of more than 5,000 businesses Australia-wide in all industry sectors compiled from 11 surveys conducted by ACCI member associations.
